en: The Eight Verses on the Auspiciousness of Śiva.
May there be auspiciousness for Bhava, for the moon-crested one, for the one devoid of qualities yet whose self is the qualities, for the death of Death, for Rudra, and for the blue-throated one;
for him who is mounted upon the bull, for the formidable one, and for him whose garment is the tiger skin.
May there be auspiciousness for you, the Lord of Beasts, the beloved of Gaurī.
(2) May there be auspiciousness for the one whose body is smeared with ashes, who wears a serpent as a sacred thread, who is adorned with a rosary of rudrākṣa beads, and whose hair is the sky. (3)
Salutations to the one whose eyes are the sun, moon, and fire; salutations to the dweller of Kailāsa;
may there be auspiciousness for the Lord of the Pramathas, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss.
Salutations to the conqueror of death, who is accompanied by Ambā, and who brings about creation, preservation, and dissolution.
May there be auspiciousness for the three-eyed one, the peaceful one, the Lord of the three worlds;
salutation to the bearer of the Gaṅgā, to the Moon, whose self is Hari and Hara.
May there be auspiciousness for the fierce one, the destroyer of Tripura, Vāmadeva.
Salutations to you, Sadyojāta, to Śarva, the bestower of the knowledge of what is to be;
salutations to you, Īśāna, the five-faced one, the auspiciousness.
Salutations to him who is the very nature of Sadāśiva, and to Tatpuruṣa.
May there be auspiciousness for Aghora, for Ghora, and for Mahādeva. 8.
May this Maṅgalāṣṭaka, composed by one impelled by Śrī Cāmuṇḍā, which is a locus of auspiciousness and bestows the desired objects of Śambhu, be read by whoever [desires it]. 9.
